chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Aban, from Is'haq ibn Ammar who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the sick person, is there a concession for him regarding the wiping (over the socks)? He said: No.

key_terms.رُخْصَةٌ: Concession or dispensation in Islamic law

ai.seo_question: Does a sick person have permission to wipe over their socks during ablution?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the concession of wiping over socks (*masah*) is not extended to the sick, distinguishing this specific ruling from the general permission granted to travelers. This highlights the principle that while illness often relaxes certain ritual obligations, the requirement to wash the feet in *wudu* remains strict unless explicitly exempted by other evidences, such as the wiping over *khuffayn* for travelers or those with specific conditions.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Aban, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the sick, ‘Is it permitted for him with regards to (neglecting) the wiping?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Aban from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of one suffering from illness if it is permissible for him to wipe for Wudu’. He (the Imam) said, ’No, it is not permissible.’”
